title: 22,000-year-old footprints in North America

tellings.quote: Graham Hanok on Ancient Apocalypse is showing footprints in North America

And those footprints in New Mexico, 23,000 year-old human footprints in New Mexico, which are interspersed with footprints of mammoths and mastodons and giant sloths and all the extinct megafauna of the Ice Age, they actually have been dated.
tellings.difference: Names New Mexico, says 23,000 rather than 22,000 years, and adds the megafauna tracks found among them.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Ice Age human footprints in North America, dated to about 22,000 to 23,000 years ago and shown by Hancock.

plain: Human footprints found in North America are said to be more than 20,000 years old, which would put people on the continent far earlier than usually thought. The writer Graham Hancock tells Michels they are "23,000 year-old human footprints in New Mexico", mixed in with tracks of mammoths, mastodons, giant sloths and other extinct Ice Age animals, and stresses that "they actually have been dated". Michels repeats it on another episode, citing Hancock's show Ancient Apocalypse and giving the age as 22,000 years.
